Hey, 
Let's try to complete the week 5 tasks. 
Check the current state, plan out the tasks [based on priority and dependency], then start the execution. 
You can be the orchestrator, and deligate the task to other models [haiku/sonet/opus] based on complexity and nature of the task.
I'll start by checking the current state — the v1.1 cycle plan in [docs/progress.md](docs/progress.md) and any open Week 5 issues — then lay out a dependency-ordered plan before executing.

result.output: 27:| **Open issues** | **29** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone (54 open repo-wide — #1111 filed AND fixed same-session; re-counted 2026-07-29 after #1110 closed #892+#912 and filed #1109, and after Batch 3's first wave — #1103/#1105/#1106 closed #919/#925/#1064 and filed #1104/#1107/#1108 — and after Batch 2 — #1100 closed #1091+#1090+#1052 (verified individually per the first-issue-only rule) and filed #1101/#1102; earlier that day #1096 closed #755 and #1098 closed #1066 — a same-day backlog-burn sweep of ~25 candidate issues against `main` found **zero** close-now issues beyond these: everything else still reproduces, evidence per-issue in the session; earlier the same day #1088/#1089/#1092/#1093/#1094/#1095 — the session filed #1085/#1086/#1087/#1090/#1091 and closed #1085/#1086/#1087/#1072/#1067) — `gh issue list --milestone 'v1.1 Backlog' --state open`; the population is stated here because the figure has silently drifted before, so **re-count it, don't decrement it**. (**2026-07-25 (later) — standing rule added + a self-inflicted register bug found and fixed.** **CONTRIBUTING rule 3a / CLAUDE.md §11: "pre-existing" is not a disposition** (user, this session) — DataQ is in prod, so a defect's age says nothing about its blast radius; every finding ends **fixed or filed**, never noted-in-a-reply or buried in a docstring. Verified-benign is a valid outcome *if the determination is recorded*; unexamined is not. Discharged immediately against my own session: two findings I had documented in code but never filed are now [#989](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/989) (`SafeMonitorError` echoes a target cell value, which its own rule forbids — bounded and arguably justified, but the redaction policy has no say in it) and [#990](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/990) (**model-vs-migration schema parity is never checked anywhere** — the test schema is `create_all`, so #457's guard covers 2 of the 3 predicate spellings, and this same gap is what let #913's mistargeted backfill migration break every fresh database). **The register bug: three PRs claimed 13 issues and closed 3.** GitHub honours only the **first** issue after a `Closes` keyword; the rest of a comma list are ignored **silently**. Ten issues sat open against shipped work — and this repo already recorded the same trap on the #720 batch, which is exactly why knowing it is not enough. All ten closed by hand with their merging PR named; the countermeasure is now structural rather than memorial — the **PR template** carries the one-keyword-per-issue rule *and* the post-merge `gh issue view` verification loop.) (**2026-07-25 — verification sweep + three closing PRs: 89 → 82 open, 15 issues resolved.** Six agents re-checked 48 candidate issues **against the tree, not the ticket** — the discipline that caught #724 the day before. **Closed on evidence, no code needed (6):** #322/#573 (both already fixed, tracked to completion under later duplicates #640/#714 — verified in-tree and re-run), #929 (subset of #787, which now carries a fresh count: **112** sites across 14 files, not the filing-time ~93), #893 (warehouse lineage WAS live-verified on both warehouses in the 07-18 arc; evidence quoted onto the issue), #731 (findings register discharged — 3 of 5 children closed, 2 tracked), #541 (**the audit is the deliverable**: both 500-risk paths are closed — `pipeline_runs` cascades, `suites.connection_id` 409s at the service layer — and the three remaining `users.id` FKs are latent by design, with the revisit trigger recorded on the issue). **Shipped (9):** [#984](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/984) docs/SAST (#729/#730/#800/#806), [#985](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/985) frontend (#915/#916/#949/#563/#601), [#986](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/986) backend (#900/#306/#728/#457). **The reviews were again worth more than the features.** #984's first attempt **broke the SAST gate**: I removed five bandit suppressions after counting *warnings* (37 → 0) instead of the gate's **exit code**, which went 0 → 5 findings. The diagnosis was wrong too — each site had TWO markers, one on the flagged node (load-bearing) and one outside its range (inert), and the `no failed test` warning names the inert one without saying which is which. All five restored, bare; the prose-tokenization half was real and stays fixed (20 warnings gone); the residual 17 are **intrinsic** to a marker on a multi-line node, so #806's "zero warnings" AC was a false premise and is recorded as such. #900's obvious fix (classify everything) was likewise wrong and **six existing tests said so** — it turned "unknown freshness column 'nope'" into "the run failed to execute", so safety is now *declared* via a `SafeMonitorError` marker rather than guessed. Reviewers also caught two places where my own text overclaimed: the #915 comment asserted `last_error`/`degraded_reason` were exclusive (they are not → [#987](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/987)), and the #457 guard's docstring claimed three coverages while checking two (the migration is never applied in the test schema) — both corrected to state the hole rather than imply it is closed. **Two lessons banked:** *judge a suppression by the gate's exit code, never its warning count* (now CONTRIBUTING rule 16), and *a subagent's `git checkout` moves YOUR HEAD* — a background review agent stranded a commit on local `main` mid-session; recovered via reflog + `cherry-pick --no-commit`, and reviewers are now told to stay read-only.) (**2026-07-24 — full open-issue triage (all 89, milestone-independent); three register entries were WRONG, each verified against the tree rather than the ticket.** [#724](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/724) (P1, orchestration-connection delete 500) was **already fixed** — migration `a3b4c5d6e7f8` + `models.py:715` + the regression test at `test_connection_service.py:350` all landed inside [#927](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/927) while addressing #753; closed. [#708](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/708) and [#748](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/748) are the **same issue filed twice** (07-08 from the #605 `runs ADD COLUMN` hang, 07-10 from the #747 `connections` hang); #708 closed into #748, which keeps the fuller record (the orphaned-backend half + the silent-`/healthz` observation), and #748's own first AC is now **partially** ticked — `lock_timeout=15s` shipped on the migrate engine (`alembic/env.py:53`, also #927) but the **bounded retry loop did not**, so a contended migrate still needs a manual retry. [#806](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/806) was **stale, not fixed**: the `_PENALTY` map it points at moved to `services/rollup.py` in the #948 unification, and a fresh `bandit -q -r backend/app` at the CI-pinned 1.9.4 emits **37** warnings, not 3, in two classes — dead suppressions across four files (`rollup.py`, `orchestration/dbt.py`, `dataset_reader.py`, `schema_drift.py`) **plus a class the ticket never described**: bandit tokenizes everything after `# nosec` as test IDs, so our own convention of writing `# nosec B105 — <prose>` emits one warning per word. Harmless to security (unknown tokens are ignored, the suppression never widens) but it is 20 lines of self-inflicted noise on the one gate an operator scans for real findings — the #828 "confident-looking nothing" class applied to SAST output. Re-scoped with the convention fix (reason on its own line above) as an AC. **Standing lesson: a P1 that has silently already been fixed costs the same attention as a real one every time the register is read.** Also re-checked and **still valid**: #601 (`frontend/.prettierignore` has no `e2e-live/.auth/` entry), #728 (the ACA host allowlist is still hardcoded at `mcp/server.py:575`), #730 (the real prod FQDN is still tracked in `CLAUDE.md`, `deploy/README.md`, `backend/tests/mcp/test_mcp_tools.py`), #541 (four FKs still lack `ondelete` — `suites.connection_id` + three `users.id` refs). **[#590](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/590)'s premise is stale and needs re-scoping, not execution:** the subscription reads `Enabled` / `PayAsYouGo` / `spendingLimit: Off`, so there is **no ~07-25 lapse** to race — the wind-down is now purely a cost decision, and until it is taken every awake resource bills real money uncapped. **[#588](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/588) is the one still on a real clock** (Snowflake trial), and #954 already records two dead prod Snowflake PATs — that leg may already be failing every scheduled run into the #419 always-alert path.) (**2026-07-24 — [#980](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/980) filed** from the `bikini/exploitarium` 0-day triage below: a Redis-8 upgrade gate, not a live defect.) (**2026-07-19 — W3 CLOSED: the four build items shipped, wind-down re-homed to W5.** #877 (CI audit gate closed with rationale), #753 → [#927](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/927), #910 → [#930](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/930), #904 → [#931](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/931), #591 → [#932](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/932); #588/#590 re-milestoned to W5 (subscription-lapse timeline, not build readiness). **The reviews were worth more than the features this session** — every one of the four found defects the green test suite did not: the #753 409 was leaking grant-scoped suite names AND `pipeline_runs` was still an unhandled-500 path for every polled orchestration connection; #910's `page` mode shipped as **dead code** while client-side throws reported "503 Service unavailable" over a healthy backend; and #904 — a watchdog written to end silent hangs — had an **unbounded Redis read on the watching thread** (#854 verbatim), a guard that **didn't work** (the non-expiring stamp let a *predecessor's* key arm it → permanent crash loop), and an `os._exit` that would abort a live GX run. All 7 fixed. **Lesson recorded: the watchdog's tests were green on all three logic bugs because every loop test ran ONE iteration against a pre-seeded state — the defects lived in state carried ACROSS iterations.** Two process misses, recorded not buried: I pushed #931 with a failing lint gate (ran ruff, saw "1 fixable", pushed anyway), and a branch switch swept #591's files into the #904 branch (caught when its tests failed on the wrong branch; commits split). Filed en route: [#925](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/925) (browse 200-cap), [#928](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/928) (`/pipeline_runs` has no paging — a loop "counted" 20,200 rows against a 211-row table because every page re-read page 1), [#929](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/929) (endemic assert-with-side-effects in wire tests).**) (**2026-07-18 night (latest) — ADR 0037: the asset access model REVERSED, one day after #920 ([#923](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/923) via [#924](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/924), user-directed).** The #920/#845/#901 identity-redaction regime described in the previous entry is **superseded**: asset identity + lineage topology (incl. column pairs) are now visible to EVERY workspace member; the health rollup is **workspace-true** (aggregated over ALL composing suites — one verdict per asset, byte-identical across viewers, pinned by a wire test); the ADR 0027 grants now guard **suite-derived detail only** (composing-suite names/runs/results/samples/incidents — suite-grain 404-no-leak intact; on the asset page hidden suites collapse to a derived restricted count). Asset detail 200s for every existing asset (asset-grain 404-no-leak retired); redacted rows / anonymous nodes / count-only column boxes deleted; lineage-source-health stake gate retired (connections were already workspace-listed). Why: the bootstrap dead-end (a new member saw only 🔒 boxes — discovery-useless) + per-viewer aggregates silently disagreeing between users (the #889 two-verdicts problem). Review batch (4 finder agents): two deploy-skew bugs fixed (old SPA bundle renders every lineage node "🔒 Restricted" without a constant `is_accessible: true` shim on LineageNodeRead — remove after one release; new SPA + old API rendered "Monitored by NaN suites" — total now derives from the workspace-true `suite_count`, one owner, no second wire field read); IncidentsPanel gained the missing "incidents from N suites outside your access are not shown" qualifier (the #828 confident-empty-state class — incidents stay granted while the page opens); one visibility derivation (`effective_permissions` labels AND lists — the second `accessible_suite_ids` round-trip and its read-race removed); single-pass `_latest_outcomes` (rollup and breakdown can't disagree about a run); malformed column-pair ENTRIES now warn (not just whole-value); dead `?? []` fallbacks removed. Deferred, filed: [#925](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/925) (the 200-row browse cap now binds against the widened all-assets population — needs paging + honest tile truncation). #889/#919 updated with the new-model implications. **Deployed + LIVE-VERIFIED same session** (images `b906490c`; migrate Succeeded): browse **byte-identical member vs admin** (22 named rows incl. `MART_ORDER_REVENUE`, yesterday's 🔒 box); member detail 200 with `suites: []` + restricted count 1 while the admin sees the suite named — the suite name provably absent from the member's wire body; UC column pairs (`comment → sentiment`) served to the member; suite-grain `GET /suites/{id}` still 404-no-leak. **The #904 post-roll beat wedge recurred on this deploy** (third occurrence): beat started 05:01:32Z then silence, `last_polled_at` frozen at the pre-roll 04:58 tick — caught by the DB-truth runbook check, cleared by a worker revision restart (ticks 05:19 + 05:29); recurrence + systematic-fix proposal recorded on #904.**) (Previous — 2026-07-18 evening — redacted browse rows shipped + live-verified ([#920](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/920) via [#921](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/921), user-directed) + the harness Snowflake-auth modernization.** Browse now INCLUDES assets monitored solely by suites outside the viewer's grants — as server-redacted rows nested in their real schema group (`DATAQ_DB → ANALYTICS → 🔒 Restricted` where the admin sees `MART_ORDER_REVENUE`): omission asserted "this schema holds nothing else", the #845 falsehood one surface over. One rule, four renderings (full row / redacted row / anonymous graph node / 404), pinned by the UPDATED three-surfaces agreement test + a wire test. The review batch mattered: accessibility now derives from the SAME `_accessible_asset_ids` helper the graph redacts with (a second SQL encoding was the #845/#847 drift class reborn); the disclosed parent path ships **pre-split** (`name_prefix_segments` — a client re-split re-detects the separator on the prefix and files the locked row in a fabricated group); `last_seen` is withheld on redacted rows (watching it tick reveals the hidden pipeline's cadence); one `isRedacted()` discriminator across tree/table/row; the dashboard's Monitored stat no longer counts redacted rows. **Live-verified as Olivia** (interactive Entra re-auth; desktop+mobile): 5 restricted rows correctly nested (ANALYTICS 1, RETAIL 3, ADLS 1 top-level — the no-parent-path shape confirmed intentional), locked rows non-navigating, wire proof `MART_ORDER_REVENUE`/`REFUNDS` appear 0 times in the payload, Monitored still 17, zero console errors. **User Q&A, recorded:** `analytics_probe_analytics_probe` = residue of the 2026-07-12 UC dbt live-verification (dbt's default schema-name concatenation doubling target+custom schema); UC's `reference` schema is absent from assets because NO signal touches it (loaded by pandas writes with no table-grain source, never read by a table-writing query) → the per-connection **inventory/catalog sync** is filed as [#919](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/919). **Harness Snowflake auth modernized (operator + agent):** the user minted a loader PAT (Snowsight; programmatic admin auth is MFA-walled) → KV `snowflake-loader-pat`, validated (`ROYARIJIT04`+`DATAQ_LOADER`), swapped into the dbt job + both Airflow apps; the `--dbt` window then built **17/17 model nodes green** (only the on-run-end GRANT hooks fail — `DATAQ_LOADER` lacks `MANAGE GRANTS`/schema ownership; one-time Snowsight fix in the harness TODO). **Honest SF-pairs status:** real table-write DML now exists (the dynamic tables), but ACCOUNT_USAGE surfaced no `directSources` within a 4h poll — the daily warehouse-lineage beat collects the column pairs automatically whenever Snowflake materializes them; nothing further is wired to wait on it. Harness re-confirmed fully down at the user's ask (5 apps Stopped, 2 ADF triggers Stopped, suspend re-issued on all 7 jobs — the read API doesn't surface suspension, so the idempotent action is the verification).) (**2026-07-18 later — the Enterprise lineage arc: prod 500 + junk-asset fallout fixed (#907/#909, #908/[#911](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/911)), a P1 broken-migration save (#913/[#914](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/914)), and the whole thing live-verified in prod by a two-identity UI pass.** The user upgraded Snowflake to **ENTERPRISE** + granted `DATAQ_READER` the ACCOUNT_USAGE read (Snowsight — programmatic admin auth is now MFA-walled), and `WAREHOUSE_LINEAGE_ENABLED` went live in prod — whereupon the first real ACCESS_HISTORY pull surfaced two defects: the asset page **500'd** (#907 — the #903 bulk upsert wrote Python `None` as JSON `null`, which passes `IS NOT NULL` and then explodes the reader; fixed in [#909](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/909) as a CLASS: `none_as_null=True` on all six nullable JSONB columns + read guards + a backfill) and the browse **flooded with junk** (#908 — the unscoped account-wide sweep materialized `SNOWPARK_TEMP_*` scratch, the dropped PERF schema, and `adf_stage_import_*` landing tables as assets). **#908's fix ([#911](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/911)) was live-tuned on real captured payloads** (the account's entire history is Stage→Table COPYs — zero table→table DML existed, which itself shaped the design) and the 8-angle agentic review found the deep defect: **the exclusive tier ladder treated two COMPLEMENTARY truths as alternatives** — OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES is the current-state VIEW graph, ACCESS_HISTORY the DML log — so a winning DML tier would have **pruned the entire dbt view chain** on the next snapshot refresh, and an all-filtered-empty pull could wipe the cache. Shipped as a **floor∪DML union** (tier names the richest contributor; empties degrade to the floor, never to a confident prunable empty; the corroboration probe died with the ambiguity it labeled) + 8 more review findings: table-like domain SET not `= 'Table'`, **OR** db-scope (a cross-db edge into scope is real lineage — dropping it is the #845-class omission), quote-aware database fold, snapshot pairs REPLACE / incremental pairs union (stale-mapping + revoked-grant-freeze fixes), the shared `MAX_COLUMN_PAIRS_PER_EDGE` cap, parse-per-distinct-blob, per-query bind assertions, SF column-grain extraction from `objects_modified[].columns[].directSources`; deferred → [#912](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/912) (Snowpark-scratch transitive stitch). **Mid-arc, the #909 deploy silently never landed:** its backfill migration targeted `checks.column_policy` — the column lives on **suites** — so `alembic upgrade head` broke on every FRESH database (caught by the main-branch E2E: the loud failure doing its job) AND the 07:22Z prod migrate execution FAILED, gating the roll (P1 [#913](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/913), fixed [#914](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/914) — safe to edit in place precisely because no environment ever recorded it applied; deliberately no existence guard, a wrong name should keep failing loudly). **Ship + verify:** one deploy carried the whole arc (migrate finally `Succeeded`, beat verified ticking per the #905 protocol); a one-shot scoped refresh pruned prod to **8 clean Snowflake edges** (floor tier, honest degrade note) + UC 6 edges / 4 with column pairs; **634 junk assets** swept via `sweep_orphan_assets` with an injected future `now` (found en route: `retention_days<=0` is the documented OFF-switch, not sweep-all); headless admin-PAT checks green (browse 22 real assets / zero junk, the ex-500 page 200s, `comment → sentiment` live in the API payload). Then a **two-identity live UI pass** (ui-tester + interactive Entra logins as **dataq-admin** and **Olivia**, desktop 1280 + mobile 390): ALL checks pass — junk-free browse (22 admin / 17 member), the ex-500 page renders for both, UC column lineage visible incl. the derived mapping, and the **#845 one-rule proven at the wire as a member**: the out-of-grant neighbour ships as `{namespace:null, name:null, env:null, is_accessible:false}` — an opaque UUID only, with the 🔒 box leaking nothing at either viewport; zero console errors anywhere. UX follow-ups filed, not dropped: [#915](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/915) (the INFO advisory conflates degraded-tier with actually-failed refreshes) + [#916](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/916) (workspace-wide advisory reads asset-scoped — copy tweak). **Honest residual:** SF **column pairs** are code-proven (tests ride the real captured Enterprise payload) but not yet live-visible — the account has never run table→table DML (everything is COPY); a `--dbt` harness window was fired to create real CTAS/dynamic-table DML — and **FAILED: Snowflake's Enterprise MFA enforcement now blocks every password-auth harness leg** (`250001: MFA authentication is required` on the dbt job; `flow_a_snowflake_load` is the same class; DataQ's own PAT-auth connection is unaffected). SF column pairs are therefore blocked on a harness-auth modernization only the operator can do (Snowsight: mint a PAT/key-pair for the loader user; steps recorded in the harness TODO) — after which the daily refresh picks the pairs up automatically (~3h ACCOUNT_USAGE lag). One un-exercisable live case remains: a redacted edge CARRYING column data (no such grant shape exists in the demo data; server+client paths test-pinned). Both prod PATs are live again post-#849 re-mint.) (**2026-07-18 — periodic QA/security sweep → prod deploy `4f8b2ae0` → a 6h silent worker outage (#905) → column-level lineage BUILT + UC live-verified (#901/#902 via [#903](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/903)).** **Sweep:** rule-4a mutation spikes on the newest code, findings filed as [#898](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/898) — `warehouse_refresh.py` **236/239 (98.7%)** once the DB-backed tests were un-skipped (mutmut's copied tree lacks `.env` → every DB-covered module silently reads "no tests"; export `TEST_DATABASE_URL` — the spike's first pass showed exactly that artifact), SF/UC providers ~65% on covered mutants (survivors: static SQL text against stub connections — accepted — plus real gaps in ladder result-shape/edge-filter assertions), frontend Stryker **81.8%** over the four assets modules (`lineageLayout.ts` 66% worst). Security scan clean across Bandit / pip-audit / pnpm-audit / **full-history** betterleaks; the one historical finding (the #849 test's original jwt.io-demo fixture, unpurgeable — force-push blocked) is fingerprint-allowlisted via `.betterleaksignore` ([#899](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/899)) so the periodic full-history scan reads zero and a real leak can't hide behind known noise; targeted #849/#852-class re-verification green (logger-level scrub incl. exported OTel attributes + rendered tracebacks, `azure.core` filter + no-propagate, span URLs path-only, classified-never-raw persistence). **Deploy** (first since 07-13; ships schema_drift #881/#883, monitor registry #880, `monitor_baselines` + warehouse-lineage migrations, warehouse-native lineage #886–#891 dark-by-default, rate-limit prefix buckets #874, 12 dep bumps): pre-checklist green (CI green on the SHA, both migrations up+down tested locally), migrate `Succeeded`, all three apps on the SHA tag, probes correct, one harness `window` (4 min): 5 mockdata jobs green + the `tr_orders_landed` event trigger ran `pl_flow_a_orders` **Succeeded on live Snowflake**, harness auto-stopped. **THEN THE WORKER WEDGED SILENTLY ([#905](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/905), P1):** a transient broker blip 50s after the roll hung the reconnect — beat never ticked ONCE for 6 hours (no retries, no exceptions, replica `Running`, telemetry frozen at 00:13Z) — the third "alive but doing nothing" incident (#852, #854 kin), detected by the telemetry frontier + console cross-check and fixed by a revision restart (beat up 06:17Z, gap recovery swept immediately, backlog dispatched 5/5). The smoke's 00:19Z ADF run was stranded outside both the 15-min poll lookback and the 1-h gap-recovery window — the #828-documented gap, recorded not re-produced. #905 carries the class fix: probeable beat liveness + loud/bounded reconnects + the workspace-wide `last_polled_at`-staleness alert. **Column lineage (#901 + the #902 ladder fix, user-directed, [#903](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/903)):** UC `system.access.column_lineage` pulled on the same watermark/window as table lineage and persisted as a `columns` JSONB **on the edge** (additive migration `a1b2c3d4e5f8`; union-merge across incremental refreshes — never forgets, never regresses to NULL; grain failure degrades with a classified note, never fails table edges), surfaced on AssetDetail with the **#845 one-rule redaction extended to columns** — an edge touching a redacted node collapses to a count-only redacted box server-side (column names are schema disclosure; pinned at the wire). The Snowflake tier ladder now **descends on authorization errors** instead of aborting (#902 — found LIVE: the GET_LINEAGE probe 002003s for a role holding only lower-tier grants like `SNOWFLAKE.GOVERNANCE_VIEWER`; skip reasons + degrade note now carry the real grant-vs-edition cause). **Live evidence:** UC verified end-to-end against the real workspace with prod-parity creds (6 table edges tier `unity_catalog_system_access` + 200 column rows captured → the committed projected fixture the tests ride); Snowflake live-blocked at the grant wall — the PAT authenticates (role-locked `DATAQ_READER`), every ACCOUNT_USAGE tier denied, admin path MFA-walled → the enable steps (Snowsight `GRANT IMPORTED PRIVILEGES` or finer `GOVERNANCE_VIEWER`, + the `WAREHOUSE_LINEAGE_ENABLED` flip) are the operator's, documented in orchestration.md. ## Finding (qa-verifier go-live workout, 2026-07-03 — non-blocking footgun)

- Frontend: a "Restore this version" button per non-current row in `CheckHistoryDrawer`, with a confirm, then refresh the editor + history.

### Notes
- Out of v1 deliberately — the roadmap line was "see previous config before overwriting" (read), and restore widens scope (confirm UX, re-validation of the restored config against the current connection — e.g. custom-SQL gating per ADR 0019).
- The snapshot already carries everything needed (`name`/`expectation_type`/`config`/thresholds); `kind` is immutable so it never changes on restore.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Restore creates a NEW version identical to the selected historical version (history preserved, no rewrite)
- [ ] Edit-permission-gated; action available in the version-history drawer; tests

=== #351 ===
Test Connection button on the New/Edit connection page (draft-connection test endpoint)
## Problem
The prototype's New-Connection **Configuration** screen has a **Test Connection** button (test before saving). The shipped app has no such button on `/connections/new` (or `/connections/:id/edit`).

Today the API can only test a **saved** connection: `POST /connections/{id}/test` reads the stored secret from the SecretStore. There is no way to probe an *unsaved* draft (the config + secret the user just typed), which is what the prototype does.

## Proposed change
**Backend** — add a draft-test endpoint that probes connectivity without persisting:
- `POST /api/v1/connections/test` taking `{ type, env?, config, secret }` → runs the existing `ConnectionAdapter` probe against the ad-hoc config/secret and returns `{ ok }` (same `ConnectionTestResult` shape).
- Reuses the adapter's existing test method; **does not** write a `connections` row or store the secret.
- Security note: a credential travels in the request body (not just the id). Keep it sync-`def`/threadpool like `/test`, never log the secret (PII redactor already covers `secret`), and gate it the same as create.

**Frontend** — add a **Test connection** button to `ConnectionForm` (create mode primarily; edit mode can reuse the saved-connection `/test`). Surface ok/failed inline like the card's health badge.

## Notes
- Surfaced during W6 Phase 4 connection-page prototype-fidelity review.
- Scope is a small backend slice + a button; can ship as its own PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test Connection works on the New/Edit page BEFORE save (draft-connection test endpoint)
- [ ] Draft secrets are not persisted by the test call; clear success/failure surface; tests

## 0. Read this first: a skill already exists for this exact task

## 1. Monitor-kind implementation: dispatch, shapes, metric_value/duration_ms/status

**Core engine:** `backend/app/datasources/monitors.py`

- Kind constants: `FRESHNESS = "freshness"` (line 45), `VOLUME = "volume"` (46), `SCHEMA_DRIFT = "schema_drift"` (47).
- **Registry pattern (#726)** — the dispatch mechanism, not an if-chain:
  - `MonitorKindStrategy` dataclass (~line 400): `kind`, `validate_config: Callable[[dict], None]`, `outcome: Callable[[scalar, config, now], CheckOutcome]`, `build_statement: Callable[[TableClause, config], Select] | None`.
  - `MONITOR_KIND_REGISTRY: dict[str, MonitorKindStrategy]` (dict literal, import-time only) — freshness/volume have a `build_statement`; `schema_drift` has `build_statement=None` (routes it to the stateful path instead of the scalar SQL path).
  - Derived tuples (also import-time, never mutated): `MONITOR_KINDS`, `SCALAR_MONITOR_KINDS` (kinds with `build_statement is not None`), `STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS` (kinds with `build_statement is None`).
- **Evaluation-function shape**:
  - `validate_config(kind, config) -> None` — raises `MonitorConfigError` (DB-free structural gate, used both at authoring time and defensively at run time).
  - `build_monitor_statement(kind, *, table, schema, catalog, config) -> Select[Any]` — SQLAlchemy Core statement (never a raw SQL string, per #476 identifier-quoting discipline); raises if the kind has no scalar-SQL form.
  - `monitor_outcome(kind, *, scalar, config, now) -> CheckOutcome` — turns the scalar aggregate result into `CheckOutcome` (`backend/app/datasources/base.py`), which carries `expectation_type`, `success`, `metric_value: float | None`, `observed_value`, `expected_value`, `sample_failures`, `errored`, `error_message`.
- **`monitor_expectation_type(kind) -> str`** — canonical `"monitor:<kind>"` string, single source of truth shared by run path, authoring, and frontend catalog.
- **Per-kind functions** (the freshness/volume "reference shape" a new `anomaly` strategy should mirror):
  - `freshness_column`, `_validate_freshness`, `_freshness_statement`, `_freshness_outcome` — metric = age in hours (`_freshness_age_hours`), higher = worse.
  - `_volume_bounds`, `_validate_volume`, `_volume_statement`, `_volume_outcome` — metric = % deviation outside `[min_rows, max_rows]` (`_volume_deviation_pct`), higher = worse.
  - `_validate_schema_drift`, `_schema_drift_outcome` — metric = drifted-column count (float), scalar is a **dict payload** (not a SQL scalar) computed by the stateful executor.
- **Run-time execution helpers**:
  - `run_monitor_specs(scalar_for, *, monitors, now)` — bands a list of `MonitorSpec`s given a scalar source; isolates a bad monitor to its own `errored` outcome (never fails siblings); routes exceptions through `classify_failure_reason` unless the exception is a `SafeMonitorError` subclass (persisted verbatim — see the `SafeMonitorError`/`MonitorConfigError` docstrings, ~lines 60-115, on what's safe to persist into `results.observed_value`/message given #900/#828/#989).
  - `evaluate_monitors(fetch_scalar, *, table, schema, catalog, monitors)` — SQL-scalar path, builds the statement then calls `fetch_scalar`.
  - `run_monitors_over_engine(engine, *, table, schema, catalog, monitors)` — the shared execution edge SQL runners (Snowflake, Unity Catalog) use: opens one connection, sources every monitor's scalar from it (#428).

**Dispatch by `check.kind` (ADR 0012 seam):** `backend/app/services/run_service.py`, function `_run_outcomes` (lines 115-226):
- `expectation_idx` → GX `CheckRunner.run_checks` (existing GX path).
- `monitor_idx = [... c.kind in SCALAR_MONITOR_KINDS]` → runner's `run_monitors` (gated by the runner's advertised `supported_monitor_kinds` capability set, line 198 — **not** `isinstance`, to avoid a Protocol name-match footgun).

**`metric_value` / `duration_ms` / status production**:

Not computed per-monitor at all currently — a new kind gets the same `NULL`.
- Status: produced by `severity.resolve_status`/`derive_status` (see §3) inside `run_service._build_result` (`backend/app/services/run_service.py:64-109`), which maps a `CheckOutcome` + the check's three thresholds to a `Result` row (`status`, `metric_value`, `observed_value`, `expected_value`, `sample_failures`).

---

## 2. `schema_drift` (#592) baseline persistence shape (PR #876) — the shape #593 (`anomaly`) must reuse

**Model:** `MonitorBaseline` in `backend/app/db/models.py:530-569`, table `monitor_baselines`.

Columns:
- `id` (UUID PK)
- `check_id` — FK `checks.id`, `ondelete="CASCADE"`, not null
- `kind` — `String(32)`, not null, **denormalized** from the check for queryability; check's own `kind` is the authority
- `baseline` — `JSONB`, not null — **kind-shaped payload**; `schema_drift` stores `{"columns": [{"name": ..., "type": ...}, ...]}`. `anomaly` (#593) is explicitly documented (line 536) to reuse this exact shape for its "metric-baseline parameters" JSONB
- `captured_at` — `DateTime(timezone=True)`, server_default `now()`
- `captured_by` — nullable FK `users.id`, `ondelete="SET NULL"`; NULL = run path captured it automatically (first run); non-NULL = manual re-baseline actor
- `created_at`, `updated_at` (standard)

Constraints (`__table_args__`, lines 548-551):
- `UniqueConstraint("check_id", name="uq_monitor_baselines_check")` — **one CURRENT baseline per check**; a re-baseline REPLACES the row (no history kept here — history lives in `results`).
- `_in_check("kind", CHECK_KINDS, "kind_valid")` — CHECK constraint against the shared `CHECK_KINDS` vocabulary (which already admits `"anomaly"`).

**Migration:** `backend/app/alembic/versions/e2f3a4b5c6d7_add_monitor_baselines.py` — creates the table exactly as above, with a **frozen copy** of `CHECK_KINDS` (line 40: `_CHECK_KINDS = ("expectation", "freshness", "volume", "schema_drift", "anomaly", "comparison")` — migrations never import live app code). Its docstring literally states: "Designed for TWO consumers: ... the W5 `anomaly` kind (#593) stores its metric baseline parameters in the same shape, so the payload is a kind-shaped JSONB — one persistence shape, no second table later." **This confirms no new migration is needed for `anomaly`'s baseline storage** — only a differently-shaped JSONB payload under the same table/columns.

**Read/write/re-baseline logic:** `backend/app/services/schema_drift.py`
- `get_baseline(session, check_id) -> MonitorBaseline | None` (select by `check_id`).
- `rebaseline(session, check) -> bool` — **deletes** the row (not an immediate recapture — avoids running introspection on the API request thread); next run recaptures live. Returns whether a row existed.
- `build_schema_drift_executor(session, *, connection, target_table, target_schema, target_catalog, secret_store, persist=True) -> Callable[[Check], CheckOutcome]` — the per-run closure pattern:
  - No baseline row → captures current snapshot, `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (constraint="uq_monitor_baselines_check")` (handles concurrent first-runs racing on READ COMMITTED without blowing up the whole run's commit), reports "baseline captured" (`success=True`, `metric_value=0.0`).
  - Baseline row exists → diff current vs stored (`diff_schemas`), band via `monitor_outcome(SCHEMA_DRIFT, scalar=payload, config=config, now=...)`.
  - `persist=False` → dry-run mode: nothing written, missing baseline previews as "would capture."
  - Introspection failure → the **check's** operational error, not the run's (one unreachable target doesn't fail siblings).

**Wiring (worker):** `backend/app/worker/tasks.py:198-210` — builds `stateful_monitor_executor` only when `any(c.kind in STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS for c in checks)`, then passes it into `run_service.execute_run(..., stateful_monitor_executor=...)`. An `anomaly` executor (`build_anomaly_executor`) would be built the same way, gated on `STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS` membership (which is automatic once registered with `build_statement=None`), and `run_service._run_outcomes` would need it threaded through similarly (it currently only accepts one `stateful_monitor_executor` param serving *all* stateful kinds via `STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS`, so both `schema_drift` and `anomaly` executors need to be composed/dispatched — check how `_run_outcomes` calls a single `stateful_monitor_executor(checks[i])` for every stateful-kind index, line 155-167 — the executor closure itself would need to branch on `check.kind` internally, or the signature needs to grow a second executor param, mirroring how `comparison_executor` is a separate param from `stateful_monitor_executor`).

---

## 3. ADR 0016 severity thresholds → status banding

**Where thresholds live:** columns on `Check` (`backend/app/db/models.py:513-515`): `warn_threshold`, `fail_threshold`, `critical_threshold` — all `Mapped[Decimal | None] = mapped_column(Numeric)`. NOT JSONB — plain nullable NUMERIC columns, one check = up to 3 thresholds, kind-agnostic (any kind can set them). Mirrored on `CheckVersion` (lines 611-613) for history snapshots.

**Banding code:** `backend/app/services/severity.py` (ADR 0016, "approach A"):
- `extract_metric(outcome: CheckOutcome) -> Decimal | None` — prefers `outcome.metric_value` (monitor kinds set this directly); else falls back to GX's `unexpected_percent` from `sample_failures`. Uses `Decimal(str(raw))` for exactness; treats non-finite (`NaN`/`inf`) as "no metric."
- `derive_status(*, success, metric_value, warn_threshold, fail_threshold, critical_threshold) -> str` — the pure banding function: `metric_value >= critical_threshold → "critical"`, else `>= fail_threshold → "fail"`, else `>= warn_threshold → "warn"`, else `"pass"`; unset thresholds treated as `+∞`; no thresholds or no metric → binary `pass`/`fail` from `success`.
- `resolve_status(outcome, *, warn_threshold, fail_threshold, critical_threshold) -> tuple[status, metric]` — the single entry point both `run_service._build_result` and `dryrun_service` call, so a dry-run preview can never disagree with what a real run would persist. `outcome.errored=True` short-circuits to `("error", None)` — no tier, no metric.

For `anomaly`, the same thresholds field reuse applies: whatever scalar the anomaly strategy's `outcome()` sets as `CheckOutcome.metric_value` (e.g. a z-score, or a deviation-from-baseline percent — "higher = worse" per the repo's stated convention) gets banded by the *same* generic `derive_status`, no new severity code needed — this is explicitly the ADR 0016 design ("the model generalizes to v1.x freshness/volume monitors ... also 'higher = worse' scalars," `docs/adr/0016-severity-derivation-semantics.md:39`).

---

## 4. Historical `metric_value` series / results table schema

**`Result` model:** `backend/app/db/models.py:696-726`, table `results`.

Columns: `id`, `run_id` (FK `runs.id`, CASCADE), `check_id` (FK `checks.id`, CASCADE), `status` (`String(16)`, CHECK-constrained to `RESULT_STATUSES`), `metric_value: Decimal | None` (`Numeric`), `duration_ms: Integer | None`, `observed_value`/`expected_value`/`sample_failures` (all `JSONB(none_as_null=True)`), `sample_failures_purged_at`, `created_at`.

Indexes (`__table_args__`, lines 698-701): `Index("ix_results_run_id", "run_id")`, `Index("ix_results_check_id", "check_id")` — no dedicated `metric_value` index; time-series queries join through `Run.created_at`.

**Existing query for a check's historical metric series** (the exact shape an anomaly baseline would build on internally, or query to compute its own rolling stats): `backend/app/services/check_service.py:842-873`, `list_check_result_history(session, suite_id, check_id, *, limit=30) -> list[CheckResultPoint]`:
```
select(Result.run_id, Result.status, Result.metric_value, Run.created_at)
  .join(Run, Result.run_id == Run.id)
  .where(Result.check_id == check_id, Run.suite_id == suite_id)
  .order_by(Run.created_at.desc())
  .limit(limit)
```
rows reversed to chronological order. Surfaced via API at `backend/app/api/v1/checks.py:336` (`list_check_result_history` endpoint). This pattern — join `results` → `runs` on `run_id`, filter `check_id` + `suite_id`, order by `Run.created_at` — is the query shape an `anomaly` monitor's baseline-refresh logic (or its own trend computation) should reuse rather than reinvent.

---

## 5. `skip` status path (#297/#298)

`RESULT_OPERATIONAL_STATUSES = ("skip", "error")` (`backend/app/db/models.py:48`) — orthogonal to the four severity tiers (`pass/warn/fail/critical`), excluded from health-score N, no penalty weight.

`skip` is a **run-level**, not a per-monitor, concept in this codebase: it means "the whole run had nothing to evaluate" (e.g., a flat-file batch hasn't landed yet), not "this one monitor kind decided to skip itself." Persistence: `backend/app/services/run_service.py:332-354`, `skip_run(session, *, run, checks, reason) -> Run` — sets `run.status = "running"` → commits every check a `Result(status="skip", observed_value={"reason": reason})` → `run.status = "succeeded"`. The run still succeeds; only its results are all `skip`.

Called from exactly one place: `backend/app/worker/tasks.py:165` — `run_service.skip_run(session, run=run, checks=checks, reason="batch_not_found")` (flat-file batch resolution failure).

Rendering: `backend/app/services/run_service.py:426-447` computes per-run `(has_error, has_skip)` flags over "operational" statuses for run-list badges; `worst_severity()` (line 65-74) explicitly never ranks `pass`/`skip`/`error`.

For `anomaly`, if a per-check "not enough baseline history yet" case should map to `skip` rather than `pass`/`error`, note that today `skip` is only produced at the whole-run granularity via `skip_run`, never per-check inside `_build_result`/`CheckOutcome`. A per-check anomaly "insufficient history" case would need either (a) a new `errored=False`/special outcome path that `_build_result` maps to `skip` per-check (not currently supported — `_build_result` only derives `error` from `outcome.errored` and the four tiers from `resolve_status`), or (b) treat it as the schema_drift precedent does for "first run" — a passing "baseline captured" result rather than a skip. Tests referencing skip: `backend/tests/integration/test_datasource_runs.py:218`, `backend/tests/services/test_run_service.py:541`, `backend/tests/worker/test_tasks.py:312`, `backend/tests/api/test_runs.py:386-389`.

**Structural (DB-free) validation:** `backend/app/datasources/monitors.py`, `validate_monitor_config(kind, config) -> None` (dispatches to `_strategy(kind).validate_config`), each kind's `_validate_<kind>` function:

An `anomaly` config (window size, sensitivity, target metric) would get its own `_validate_anomaly(config: dict[str, Any]) -> None` here, raising `MonitorConfigError` on bad shape, then registered as the `validate_config` field of its `MonitorKindStrategy` entry.

You are implementing the BACKEND of GitHub issue #593 — the `anomaly` monitor kind — in the DataQ repo (you are in an isolated git worktree of /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ). This is the Week-5 P1 headline feature.

MANDATORY FIRST READS (in order):
1. `.claude/skills/new-monitor-kind/SKILL.md` — a purpose-built traversal guide for adding exactly this kind. Follow its checklist end-to-end (registry → run path → authoring → dimension → surfaces → docs → tests), EXCEPT the frontend-catalog steps: the authoring UI ships in a separate stacked PR — do NOT touch frontend/src in this PR, and do NOT regenerate the catalog fixture.
2. `docs/adr/0012-monitor-kind-seam.md` and `docs/adr/0016-severity-derivation-semantics.md`.
3. Issue #593 body (`gh issue view 593`).
4. `backend/app/services/schema_drift.py` — the stateful-kind reference implementation, and `backend/app/datasources/monitors.py` — the registry.

## Design brief (decided by the orchestrator — follow it; flag disagreements in your report rather than silently deviating)

**Model: deliberately simple + explainable. Rolling-window z-score, optional day-of-week seasonality, no ML dependency.**

- `anomaly` is a **stateful** kind: register a `MonitorKindStrategy` with `build_statement=None` so it lands in `STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS` and routes through the stateful-executor path like `schema_drift`.
- **Self-contained measurement** (no cross-check coupling, no within-run ordering hazard): each run, the anomaly executor measures a raw scalar itself against the target table, chosen by `config.target_metric`:
  - `"row_count"` — reuse the volume kind's SQL statement builder (COUNT(*)).
  - `"freshness_age_hours"` — reuse the freshness statement builder + age math (optional `column` config like freshness).
  Reuse the existing `_volume_statement`/`_freshness_statement`-style builders and the shared quoting discipline — do NOT hand-roll SQL strings (#476/#937).
- **Baseline** persists in the existing `monitor_baselines` table (NO new migration — the table + its migration docstring were designed for this). JSONB payload (kind-shaped), e.g.:
  `{"version": 1, "target_metric": "row_count", "window": 14, "seasonality": false, "observations": [{"ts": "<iso8601 utc>", "value": 123.0}, ...]}` — a rolling window of raw observations, trimmed to the configured window on every update. With `seasonality: true`, scoring uses only observations from the same day-of-week as `now` (UTC); the window then means "last N same-weekday observations" — size the trim accordingly (keep up to window*7 raw observations, or per-weekday buckets — your call, document it).
- **Evaluation each run** (in the executor closure, mirroring `build_schema_drift_executor`):
  1. Measure raw scalar x.
  2. Load baseline row. Compute the eligible prior observations (same weekday only if seasonality).
  3. If eligible count < `min_points` (config, default 7, min 3): **cold start** → outcome that persists as a per-check `Result(status="skip")` with an explanatory observed_value (e.g. {"reason": "insufficient_history", "points": k, "min_points": n}) — never a fake pass/fail. See "per-check skip" below.
  4. Else compute mean/stddev of prior observations; z = |x - mean| / stddev. Degenerate stddev == 0: if x == mean → z = 0; else treat as maximally anomalous in a DOCUMENTED way (e.g. cap at a large sentinel like 99.0) — pick something explainable, never a division crash or NaN/inf (severity.extract_metric treats non-finite as "no metric" — don't hand it one).
  5. `CheckOutcome.metric_value = z` (the deviation score, "higher = worse"), `observed_value` = explainable payload {value, mean, stddev, points, window, seasonality, target_metric}, `success` = (z < fail-or-first-set-threshold? NO —) leave success semantics to the thresholds: set `success=True` and let ADR-0016 `resolve_status` band z through warn/fail/critical exactly like other monitors do (check how _freshness_outcome/_volume_outcome set success vs thresholds and be consistent with that established pattern).
  6. Append x to observations, trim to window, upsert the baseline row (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT the `uq_monitor_baselines_check` constraint — mirror schema_drift's race handling; for updates a plain UPDATE on the loaded row is fine).
  7. `persist=False` (dry-run mode) → measure + score but never write the baseline.
- **Config schema** (validated in a new `_validate_anomaly` in monitors.py, registered as the strategy's validate_config): `target_metric` required ∈ {row_count, freshness_age_hours}; `column` optional identifier (only meaningful for freshness_age_hours — validate with the same `_ident` discipline); `window` optional int default 14, bounds [3, 90]; `min_points` optional int default 7, bounds [3, window]; `seasonality` optional bool default false. Next run recaptures from scratch (cold start applies again — that is correct and explainable).
- **Per-check `skip`**: today `skip` is only produced run-level via `skip_run`. `RESULT_STATUSES` already admits skip per-row. Report the evidence tail when done.

input.message:
Your branch is pushed as PR #1114. The review found one real issue to fix (confirmed with repros by two independent reviewers):

Sharing runsState means PipelineRunsTab's 30s poll (armed permanently once that tab is visited — antd keeps panes mounted) can flip the shared state to 'error' on a transient background failure, and RunsTab's `if (state.status === 'error') return <PageError/>` then replaces the whole Runs table+filters with a full-page error — while PipelineRunsTab handles the same failure with a graceful inline Alert (runsJoinFailed). Pre-PR, a poll failure was cosmetic.

Fix on the same branch in your worktree:
1. Make a background refetch failure non-catastrophic for RunsTab. Preferred shape: only render PageError when there is NO last-good data (initial load failure); when data was previously loaded and a background reload fails, keep rendering the last-good table with an inline warning Alert (mirror the runsJoinFailed pattern/copy). Check what useAsyncData does to `data` on a failed reload — if it clears data on error, you may need to retain last-good data (either in the hook if that's its documented contract-compatible evolution, or locally in the parent). Choose the minimal change consistent with useAsyncData's documented contract; do NOT regress its "no flash to loading" behavior.
2. Also pass `onRetry` so the initial-load PageError isn't a dead end (repo convention: Assets.tsx/AssetDetail.tsx pass onRetry={reload}).
3. Add a test: visit Pipeline tab (arm poll), return to Runs, fail the next poll tick → Runs table still shows last-good rows + inline warning; and a test that initial-load failure still shows PageError.
4. Re-run lint/format/typecheck/tests. Commit as `fixup:` (no amend/force-push) and `git push`.

Report evidence tails when done.

+"""anomaly monitor kind — the stateful z-score engine (#593, ADR 0012).
+
+The model is **deliberately simple and explainable** (issue #593): a rolling
+window of the check's own raw measurements, a mean/stddev over it, and the
+absolute z-score of this run's value as the ADR-0016-banded ``metric_value``.
+No ML dependency, no opaque state — every number behind a verdict is written to
+``observed_value``, which is what makes the learned band drawable (and arguable
+with) on the metric-trend view (#594).
+
+The pieces:
+
+* :func:`measure_metric` — the raw scalar this run observed. It reuses the
+  freshness/volume Core statement builders and their driver-boundary
+  normalisation, so an anomaly over row count measures exactly what a volume
+  monitor counts, quoted by the connection's own dialect (#476/#937).
+* :func:`eligible_values` / :func:`score` / :func:`build_score_payload` — the
+  pure scoring, unit-testable with no datasource and no DB.
+* :func:`build_anomaly_executor` — the per-run closure the worker injects into
+  ``run_service._run_outcomes`` (the #592/#794 pattern): it owns the session and
+  the baseline row. Runners never see stateful kinds — they have no DB.
+
+**Self-contained by design.** The measurement is taken by this executor against
+the suite's target, *not* read from a sibling freshness/volume check's result.
+Coupling to another check would make the anomaly depend on that check existing,
+still being enabled, and having already run within the same run — a within-run
+ordering hazard for a value the executor can simply measure itself.
+
+**Cold start is a `skip`, never a verdict.** Below ``min_points`` usable prior
+observations there is nothing to compare against; the check reports the
+operational ``skip`` status (#122) with the point count, so "not watching yet" is
+visible instead of being laundered into a green pass.
+
+Baseline payload (JSONB, `monitor_baselines.baseline`), version 1::
+
+    {"version": 1, "target_metric": "row_count", "window": 14,
+     "seasonality": false,
+     "observations": [{"ts": "2026-07-30T02:00:00+00:00", "value": 32840.0}, ...]}
+
+Observations are raw measurements in chronological order, trimmed on every
+update to `AnomalyParams.retained_observations`. They are metadata about a
+measurement, never row data — no PII, no retention-sweep involvement.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import math
+import statistics
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from datetime import UTC, datetime
+from typing import Any
+
+from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

+from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
+from backend.app.core.secrets import SecretStore
+from backend.app.datasources.base import CheckOutcome
+from backend.app.datasources.monitors import (
+    ANOMALY,
+    ANOMALY_DEGENERATE_Z,
+    FRESHNESS,
+    ROW_COUNT_METRIC,
+    VOLUME,
+    AnomalyParams,
+    MonitorConfigError,
+    SafeMonitorError,
+    anomaly_params,
+    build_monitor_statement,
+    freshness_age_hours,
+    monitor_expectation_type,
+    monitor_outcome,
+    row_count_from_scalar,
+)
+from backend.app.db.models import Check, Connection, MonitorBaseline
+from backend.app.services.failure_classifier import classify_failure_reason
+from backend.app.services.monitor_baseline import get_baseline, insert_baseline_if_absent
+from backend.app.services.profile_service import ProfileUnsupportedError, _open_connection
+
+log = get_logger(__name__)
+
+# Bump only alongside a real payload-shape change; an unrecognised version is
+# treated as "no usable history" (cold start) rather than mis-read — a wrong
+# baseline is worse than a slow one.
+BASELINE_VERSION = 1
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Observation:
+    """One recorded measurement: when it was taken (UTC) and what it was."""
+
+    ts: datetime
+    value: float
+
+
+# ───────────────────────── measurement ─────────────────────────
+
+
+def measure_metric(
+    connection: Connection,
+    *,
+    table: str,
+    schema: str | None,
+    catalog: str | None,
+    params: AnomalyParams,
+    secret_store: SecretStore,
+    now: datetime,
+) -> float:
+    """This run's raw measurement of the configured ``target_metric``.
+
+    ``row_count`` reuses the volume kind's ``SELECT COUNT(*)``; ``freshness_age_hours``
+    reuses the freshness kind's ``SELECT MAX(<column>)`` plus the shared age math.
+    Both come back as a **Core statement**, executed uncompiled so the connection's
+    own dialect quotes the identifiers (#476/#937) — hand-rolling the SQL here would
+    re-introduce the mixed-case fold bug on Snowflake and the wrong quote character
+    on Unity Catalog.
+
+    SQL datasources only, which is why `check_service.ANOMALY_CAPABLE_TYPES` is
+    narrower than `MONITOR_CAPABLE_TYPES`. Iceberg and flat files compute their
+    monitor scalars natively *inside their runners*, and a stateful kind never
+    reaches a runner — extending anomaly to them is a per-datasource measurement
+    seam on this function, not a widened allowlist. The defence-in-depth check
+    below restates that as the check's own error rather than letting a
+    non-SQL connection surface as an unexplained classified failure.
+    """
+    if params.target_metric == ROW_COUNT_METRIC:
+        statement = build_monitor_statement(
+            VOLUME, table=table, schema=schema, catalog=catalog, config={}
+        )
+    else:
+        statement = build_monitor_statement(
+            FRESHNESS, table=table, schema=schema, catalog=catalog, config={"column": params.column}
+        )
+    try:
+        with _open_connection(connection, secret_store) as conn:
+            scalar = conn.execute(statement).scalar()
+    except ProfileUnsupportedError as exc:
+        raise MonitorConfigError(
+            f"anomaly monitors need a SQL datasource, not {connection.type!r}"
+        ) from exc
+    if params.target_metric == ROW_COUNT_METRIC:
+        return float(row_count_from_scalar(scalar))
+    source = f"MAX({params.column})"
+    if scalar is None:
+        # An empty table (or an all-NULL column) has no age. Same call as the
+        # freshness kind makes, and for the same reason: silently scoring a
+        # missing measurement would poison the baseline with a fabricated point.
+        raise MonitorConfigError(f"{source} is unavailable, anomaly can't measure freshness age")
+    return freshness_age_hours(scalar, now=now, source=source, column=params.column)
+
+
+# ───────────────────────── baseline payload ─────────────────────────
+
+
+def load_observations(row: MonitorBaseline | None, params: AnomalyParams) -> list[Observation]:
+    """The usable prior observations from a stored baseline row.
+
+    Returns ``[]`` — i.e. a fresh cold start — when the row is absent, was written
+    by a future payload version, or was recorded for a **different**
+    ``target_metric``. That last case matters: row counts and staleness hours are
+    different quantities in different units, so scoring one against the other's
+    history would produce a confident number about nothing. Editing the check's
+    target metric therefore restarts learning, which is the honest behaviour.
+
+    Malformed or non-finite entries are dropped individually rather than failing
+    the check: the surviving history is still a valid baseline, and a monitor that
+    errors because one JSONB row is odd is worse than one that learns from the rest.
+    """
+    if row is None:
+        return []
+    payload = row.baseline if isinstance(row.baseline, dict) else {}
+    if payload.get("version") != BASELINE_VERSION:
+        return []
+    if payload.get("target_metric") != params.target_metric:
+        return []
+    raw = payload.get("observations")
+    if not isinstance(raw, list):
+        return []
+    out: list[Observation] = []
+    for entry in raw:
+        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
+            continue
+        value = entry.get("value")
+        if not isinstance(value, (int, float)) or isinstance(value, bool):
+            continue
+        if not math.isfinite(value):
+            continue
+        try:
+            ts = datetime.fromisoformat(str(entry.get("ts")))
+        except (TypeError, ValueError):
+            continue
+        out.append(Observation(ts=ts if ts.tzinfo else ts.replace(tzinfo=UTC), value=float(value)))
+    return out
+
+
+def dump_baseline(observations: list[Observation], params: AnomalyParams) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """The JSONB payload for a set of observations (already trimmed by the caller)."""
+    return {
+        "version": BASELINE_VERSION,
+        "target_metric": params.target_metric,
+        "window": params.window,
+        "seasonality": params.seasonality,
+        "observations": [{"ts": o.ts.isoformat(), "value": o.value} for o in observations],
+    }
+
+
+def trim(observations: list[Observation], params: AnomalyParams) -> list[Observation]:
+    """Keep only the most recent `retained_observations` (chronological order in)."""
+    retained = params.retained_observations
+    return observations[-retained:] if retained else []
+
+
+# ───────────────────────── scoring (pure) ─────────────────────────
+
+
+def eligible_values(
+    observations: list[Observation], *, now: datetime, params: AnomalyParams
+) -> list[float]:
+    """The prior values this run is scored against, newest-last.
+
+    With ``seasonality`` on, only observations sharing ``now``'s **UTC weekday**
+    count — so a Monday-morning load that is always three times Sunday's isn't
+    reported as an anomaly every Monday. The window then means "the last N
+    same-weekday observations", which is why the retained history is seven times
+    larger in that mode. UTC (not a local zone) because every stored ``ts`` is
+    UTC and the alternative — a per-check timezone — is config nobody asked for.
+    """
+    considered = (
+        [o for o in observations if o.ts.weekday() == now.weekday()]
+        if params.seasonality
+        else list(observations)
+    )
+    return [o.value for o in considered[-params.window :]]
+
+
+def score(value: float, priors: list[float]) -> tuple[float, float, float, bool]:
+    """``(z_score, mean, stddev, degenerate)`` for a value against its priors.
+
+    The **sample** standard deviation (n-1) — the priors are a sample of the
+    metric's behaviour, not its whole population — which is why the config floor
+    on ``min_points`` is 3 rather than 1.
+
+    ``stddev == 0`` (every prior identical) has no defined z. It is resolved
+    explicitly, not by arithmetic: an identical value is ``0.0`` (nothing moved),
+    and any other value is :data:`ANOMALY_DEGENERATE_Z`, a documented finite
+    sentinel. Dividing would raise, and ``inf``/``nan`` would be dropped by
+    ``severity.extract_metric`` as "no bandable metric" — i.e. maximal deviation
+    silently resolving to ``pass``.
+    """
+    if len(priors) < 2:
+        raise MonitorConfigError(
+            f"anomaly scoring needs at least 2 prior points, got {len(priors)}"
+        )
+    mean = statistics.fmean(priors)
+    stddev = statistics.stdev(priors)

+    if stddev == 0.0:
+        return (0.0 if value == mean else ANOMALY_DEGENERATE_Z), mean, stddev, True
+    return abs(value - mean) / stddev, mean, stddev, False
+
+
+def build_score_payload(value: float, priors: list[float], params: AnomalyParams) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """The `observed_value` payload the registry's outcome strategy bands.
+
+    Everything the verdict rests on is in it — the measurement, the learned
+    mean/stddev, how many points were used and whether seasonality filtered them
+    — so a surprising `critical` can be explained from the stored result alone.
+    """
+    payload: dict[str, Any] = {
+        "target_metric": params.target_metric,
+        "value": value,
+        "points": len(priors),
+        "window": params.window,
+        "min_points": params.min_points,
+        "seasonality": params.seasonality,
+    }
+    if len(priors) < params.min_points:
+        payload["insufficient_history"] = True
+        payload["reason"] = "insufficient_history"
+        return payload
+    z_score, mean, stddev, degenerate = score(value, priors)
+    payload.update(
+        {
+            "z_score": round(z_score, 6),
+            "mean": round(mean, 6),
+            "stddev": round(stddev, 6),
+            "deviation": round(value - mean, 6),
+            "degenerate_stddev": degenerate,
+        }
+    )
+    return payload
+
+
+# ───────────────────────── run executor ─────────────────────────
+
+
+def build_anomaly_executor(
+    session: Session,
+    *,
+    connection: Connection,
+    target_table: str,
+    target_schema: str | None,
+    target_catalog: str | None,
+    secret_store: SecretStore,
+    persist: bool = True,
+) -> Callable[[Check], CheckOutcome]:
+    """A per-run executor for `anomaly` checks (the #592/#794 stateful pattern).
+
+    Each call measures the target, scores it against the check's own rolling
+    history, appends the measurement, and upserts the baseline. First runs (and
+    any run still short of ``min_points``) report `skip` while still **recording**
+    the observation — that is how the history accrues.
+
+    ``persist=False`` is the dry-run mode: measure and score, write nothing.
+    A measurement or config failure is the CHECK's operational error (#122),
+    never the run's — one unreachable target must not fail sibling checks.
+    """
+
+    def executor(check: Check) -> CheckOutcome:
+        config = dict(check.config)
+        now = datetime.now(UTC)
+        try:
+            params = anomaly_params(config)
+            value = measure_metric(
+                connection,
+                table=target_table,
+                schema=target_schema,
+                catalog=target_catalog,
+                params=params,
+                secret_store=secret_store,
+                now=now,
+            )
+        except Exception as exc:
+            # Safe-marked messages (bad config, an unparseable timestamp cell)
+            # name the user's own mistake and persist verbatim; anything else —
+            # a driver/SDK exception, which can carry a DSN or a SAS-signed URL
+            # (#828/#900) — is classified before it reaches a result row.
+            log.warning(
+                "anomaly_measurement_failed",
+                check_id=str(check.id),
+                connection_type=connection.type,
+                error_type=type(exc).__name__,
+            )
+            return CheckOutcome(
+                expectation_type=monitor_expectation_type(ANOMALY),
+                success=False,
+                errored=True,
+                error_message=(
+                    str(exc) if isinstance(exc, SafeMonitorError) else classify_failure_reason(exc)
+                ),
+            )
+        row = get_baseline(session, check.id)
+        observations = load_observations(row, params)
+        priors = eligible_values(observations, now=now, params=params)
+        payload = build_score_payload(value, priors, params)
+        if row is not None:
+            payload["baseline_captured_at"] = row.captured_at.isoformat()
+        if persist:
+            kept = trim([*observations, Observation(ts=now, value=value)], params)
+            baseline = dump_baseline(kept, params)
+            if row is None:
+                insert_baseline_if_absent(
+                    session, check_id=check.id, kind=ANOMALY, baseline=baseline
+                )
+            else:
+                row.baseline = baseline
+        else:
+            payload["dry_run"] = True
+        return monitor_outcome(ANOMALY, scalar=payload, config=config, now=now)
+
+    return executor

## Finding (from the /code-review of PR #1116, scored 60 — pre-existing class, filed rather than fixed in-PR)

`_extra_secrets(config, secret_store)` resolves ANY `*_secret_name` field in a connection config against the flat SecretStore namespace and hands the plaintext to `adapter.test()`. Config is user-supplied on the create path and now also on the draft-test path (#1116), and `GET /connections` exposes every connection's config (single-tenant, connection-unscoped by design), so any authenticated user can:

1. Read a victim connection's `catalog_secret_name` off `GET /connections`.
2. `POST /connections/test` (or create+test) with `type=iceberg`, `catalog_uri` pointed at an attacker-controlled host, and the victim's `catalog_secret_name`.
3. The server resolves the victim's real catalog credential and `inject_uri_password()` sends it to the attacker's endpoint — SSRF + credential exfiltration.

The **class is pre-existing** (`test_connection` on a saved row has always resolved `_extra_secrets`, and create accepts arbitrary config at the same auth gate); the draft-test endpoint adds a **trace-less variant** (no persisted row). Under the current single-tenant workspace-trusted model this is an accepted-risk shape, but it becomes a real boundary violation the moment RBAC (#740–#744) introduces users who should NOT be able to wield every stored credential.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decide the mitigation: (a) `*_secret_name` in a test/create payload may only reference a secret already attached to a connection the caller may access, or (b) draft-test refuses `*_secret_name` resolution entirely, or (c) explicitly record accepted-risk-until-RBAC with a pointer from ADR 0033.
- [ ] Whatever is chosen covers BOTH the saved-connection test and the draft test.
- [ ] Regression test proving a foreign `*_secret_name` cannot be exfiltrated once mitigated (or the accepted-risk record).

Refs #1116, ADR 0011, ADR 0033 (#740–#744).

Instead I extracted the validation branching update_check uses into a shared `_validate_kind_specific_config` (dispatches to `validate_monitor_check`/`validate_comparison_check`/`validate_custom_sql_check`/`validate_expectation_check` by kind) and the commit/versioning/409-race-handling into `_record_version_and_commit`. `update_check` now calls both; `restore_check_version` calls the same validators then applies every snapshot field unconditionally (including clearing to `None`), so a kind added later automatically covers restore too — not a hand-picked validator subset.

- `backend/app/services/check_service.py` — `CheckVersionNotFoundError`, `_validate_kind_specific_config`, `_record_version_and_commit`, `restore_check_version`; `update_check` refactored to reuse both helpers (behavior-preserving).
- `backend/app/api/v1/checks.py` — `POST /suites/{suite_id}/checks/{check_id}/versions/{version_no}/restore`, edit-gated.
- `backend/tests/api/test_checks.py` — 9 new tests: additive history, no-op on current-version restore, unknown version/check 404, authz (viewer 403/outsider 404/editor 200), and two invalid-snapshot 422 cases (legacy reversed thresholds, legacy non-read-only custom SQL) with live-check-untouched assertions.

- Frontend tests updated/added in `CheckHistoryDrawer.test.tsx` and `CheckEdit.test.tsx`.

**Gate results:** backend black/ruff/mypy/bandit clean; 3220/3220 backend tests pass, 97.00% coverage. Frontend lint/format/typecheck clean; 704/704 tests pass, 90.36% lines coverage (both above the 80% CI gates).

Your branch is pushed as PR #1122. The review confirmed two items — fix both, `fixup:` commit, plain push:

2. **SnoozedTag parity**: the interactive ResultsTable renders `<SnoozedTag check={check}/>` beside the check name ("a muted check must say so, or the operator wastes time asking why no alert arrived", #653) — the printed report omits it, so a snoozed failing check prints as a bare fail with no suppression indicator. Add an equivalent textual marker in the report's check column (print-friendly text like "(snoozed)" — reuse whatever predicate SnoozedTag uses; a plain text suffix is fine for print). Add a test.

"""Live driver-boundary probe for the anomaly kind (#593, feature-matrix ⏳→✅ evidence).

Runs anomaly.measure_metric — the exact code path where a Decimal COUNT or a str
TIMESTAMP crosses the driver boundary (#953/#520 class) — against the two live
warehouses, plus build_score_payload over the measured values. Secrets resolve
via AzureKeyVaultStore at call time; nothing is printed but shapes and numbers.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from types import SimpleNamespace

from backend.app.core.secrets import AzureKeyVaultStore
from backend.app.datasources.monitors import anomaly_params
from backend.app.services.anomaly import build_score_payload, measure_metric

VAULT = "https://dataq-app-kv-aw6laj.vault.azure.net/"
store = AzureKeyVaultStore(VAULT)
now = datetime.now(UTC)

SF = SimpleNamespace(
    type="snowflake",
    config={
        "account": "PVQSOEQ-ZGB34383",
        "user": "ROYARIJIT04",
        "database": "DATAQ_DB",
        "schema": "RETAIL",
        "warehouse": "DATAQ_WH",
        "role": "DATAQ_READER",
    },
    secret_ref="conn-snowflake-retail-dev-6729c4f9",
)

UC = SimpleNamespace(
    type="unity_catalog",
    config={
        "workspace_url": "https://dbc-4492dde4-090c.cloud.databricks.com",
        "warehouse_id": "b6403b6e3734f0ce",
    },
    secret_ref="conn-unity-catalog-dataq-retail-dev-ae7b09b7",
)


def probe(name, conn, table, schema, catalog, ts_column):
    p_rc = anomaly_params({"target_metric": "row_count"})
    rc = measure_metric(
        conn, table=table, schema=schema, catalog=catalog, params=p_rc,
        secret_store=store, now=now,
    )
    print(f"{name} row_count: value={rc!r} type={type(rc).__name__}")
    p_fr = anomaly_params({"target_metric": "freshness_age_hours", "column": ts_column})
    age = measure_metric(
        conn, table=table, schema=schema, catalog=catalog, params=p_fr,
        secret_store=store, now=now,
    )
    print(f"{name} freshness_age_hours({ts_column}): value={age!r} type={type(age).__name__}")
    # Pure scoring over a synthetic prior window seeded from the live value —
    # proves the measured floats feed the score path without type surprises.
    payload = build_score_payload(rc, [rc * 0.98, rc * 1.01, rc * 0.99, rc, rc * 1.02, rc * 0.97, rc], p_rc)
    print(f"{name} score payload: z={payload.get('z_score')} points={payload['points']}")
    assert isinstance(rc, float) and isinstance(age, float) and age >= 0.0
    return rc, age


ok = True
for args in (
    ("snowflake", SF, "ORDERS", "RETAIL", None, "ORDER_TS"),
    ("unity_catalog", UC, None, None, None, None),  # placeholder — filled below
):
    if args[0] == "unity_catalog":
        continue
    try:
        probe(*args)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        ok = False
        print(f"{args[0]} FAILED: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")

sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

PR #1122's Playwright CI job failed — the print-only RunReport DOM duplicates strings for the e2e specs the same way it did for Vitest, and Playwright strict mode rejects the ambiguous locator:

- e2e/results.spec.ts:16 "lists seeded runs and drills into the severity-spread run": line ~33 `page.getByText('order_id not null')` resolves to 2 elements (`getByTestId('rd-screen')` copy + `getByTestId('run-report')` <td>).
- e2e/results.spec.ts:58 "drills into the operational-spectrum run (critical / error / skip)": same class.

Fix in frontend/e2e/results.spec.ts: scope the affected run-detail assertions to `page.getByTestId('rd-screen')` (the testid you already added), consistent with the Vitest screenRegion approach. Audit the WHOLE e2e directory for other run-detail-page getByText/getByRole assertions that could now double-resolve (check-editor.spec.ts run-detail steps, run-detail variants specs from #527) — scope any at-risk ones in the same pass rather than letting CI find them one at a time. Playwright runs locally via `pnpm exec playwright test` with the dev stack (check .github/workflows for how CI launches it — if you can run the two failing specs locally, do; if the harness is impractical locally, rely on scoping + CI). Commit as `fixup:`, plain push. Report what you scoped.
